s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic sinusitis with destruction of nasal structures and recurrent infections
salient_findings: Crusting and irritation of the sinuses
Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates
key_facts: Male patient in his 60s
Denies hemoptysis, dyspnea, fatigue, or weight loss
No prior sinus surgeries or history of nasal trauma
Occasional use of nasal irrigation with tap water
Normal laboratory tests for C-reactive protein, erythrocyte sedimentation rate, angiotensin-converting enzyme, white blood cell count, and antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody panel
Negative HIV test
Substantial septal deformity with near complete destruction of the sinus septate on CT
Thinning of the posterior wall of the frontal sinuses and erosion of the bone near the right lacrimal system on CT
Enlarged lymph nodes in the mediastinum on Chest CT
Sinus mucosa showed noncaseating granulomas
Initial AFB staining was negative
Culture showed growth of Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas
AFB PCR probe of hilar lymph node was positive
Second FESS AFB PCR probe was positive

shortlist.label: Tuberculosis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive AFB PCR probe and noncaseating granulomas

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Noncaseating granulomas and normal laboratory tests

shortlist.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
shortlist.why_kept: Destruction of nasal structures and recurrent infections

shortlist.label: Midline destructive granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Destruction of septal cartilage and turbinates

shortlist.label: Fungal sinusitis
shortlist.why_kept: Culture showed growth of Pseudomonas and Staphylococcus aureus, and patient's use of nasal irrigation with tap water

raw.rationale: The presence of noncaseating granulomas in the sinus mucosa and the positive AFB PCR probe results from both the hilar lymph node and the second FESS are strong evidence for tuberculosis, despite the initial negative AFB staining.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can cause granulomas, the positive AFB PCR probe results point more specifically to tuberculosis.

rejected.label: Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
rejected.why: This condition typically presents with a positive ANCA panel and more systemic symptoms, which are not present in this case.

rejected.label: Midline destructive granuloma
rejected.why: This diagnosis does not account for the positive AFB PCR probe results or the systemic findings like enlarged mediastinal lymph nodes.

rejected.label: Fungal sinusitis
rejected.why: The culture results showing Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas, along with the lack of specific evidence for fungal infection, make this diagnosis less likely.
